ety.text: Inherited from Middle French ronfler, from Old French ronfler, an expressive word of onomatopoetic origin. Compare Piedmontese romfé, Lombard romfà, Emilian romfè.

From (a variant?) of trayant (here meaning "pulling, dragging"), the present participle of traire, which in the Middle Ages would have especially been in reference to a pitchfork for handling manure, but also to a fishing net. The term was a nickname given to the user of either tool.
